tech_stack.web: Spring WebFlux (reactive, Mono/Flux, no blocking I/O)
tech_stack.persistence: Spring Data R2DBC + Flyway migrations (embedded H2 only for boot/test)

integration.Telemetry Ingestion & Validation -> Tele: in-process reactive stream (Flux) of TelemetrySampleValidated/ValidationFailed events via a published port; bounded buffers with backpressure
same published validation events consumed through a port; store appends as-is
integration.Telemetry Stream Reconciliation -> Telem: TelemetryBackfillReordered consumed to append Event Revisions
integration.Telemetry Stream Reconciliation -> exter: TelemetryWindowEmitted published on a backpressure-aware stream port; the out-of-process consumer boundary (downstream analytics streams) is external and declared here
integration.external -> Telemetry Ingestion & Valida: anticorruption layer translating device Ingress Packets into Telemetry Samples at the WebFlux entry point

risks: Packets later than the 60s backfill window are unspecified; assumed appended as Event Revisions by the store
Unbounded buffers under burst load; all buffers and windows must be bounded and configured via externalized keys
Ordering must use t_device, never t_ingress; clock skew on devices is not handled
Consumers must be idempotent (eventual consistency, redelivery possible)
TelemetryRevisionAppended has no consumer in this slice
H2 reserves 'value'; embedded test schema must use NON_KEYWORDS=VALUE or quoted columns
Storage technology unspecified; reactive relational store assumed, append-only enforced at port and schema level
Throughput targets are unspecified; thresholds (boundaries, window size, buffer capacity) must be configuration, not magic numbers

drivers: Telemetry Event Store owns durable raw time-series records; other contexts hold only in-memory windowed state
persistence.storage_paradigm: Append-only relational time-series log (no updates or deletes) with revision records

aggregates: TelemetryRecord (immutable raw sample with validation status, t_device, t_ingress, revision number)
data_model.identity: sample identity (device, metric, t_device) plus monotonically increasing revision
data_model.append_only_rule: corrections and backfills append a new revision; existing rows are never mutated

queries: Latest revision per sample by device and metric within a t_device range
Full revision history of a sample (audit)
persistence.migration_plan: Expand-only versioned migrations; indexes on (device, metric, t_device, revision); append-only audit_trail table; embedded in-process substitute for boot tests
persistence.backup_recovery: Platform-level periodic snapshots plus log-based recovery; immutability makes replay safe
open_questions: Retention period and partitioning of raw history

observability.correlation_key: requestId (adopted from inbound header or generated per ingress packet); carried explicitly in audit entries and reactive context
step_logs: ingress packet accepted (count of samples, outcome)

audit_trail.port: AuditTrail.record(AuditEntry) in application layer; append-only infrastructure adapter; migration owned by database step
audit_trail.semantics: all fields non-null; actor is the device/source or system component; best-effort async unless the append joins the same reactive chain

observability.tag_policy: bounded enumerations only; never deviceId or sample ids

logs.sink: local append-only rolling JSON-lines file (logs/telemetry-ingestion-processing.log) shipped by platform agent (Filebeat/Elastic Agent)
logs.rolling: size and history bounded via config keys

export.metrics: Micrometer via actuator; no scrape endpoint or push unless later named
export.dependency_rule: no runtime dependency on the external tool; boot test passes with it absent

observability.config_literals: levels, formats, sampling and sink destination/rolling live in the configuration unit
